newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lawyers drop request to quit Singapore libel case.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers drop request to quit Singapore libel case.

text.p: Lawyers acting for a Singapore opposition politician in 13 defamation suits filed by members of the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) have reversed their decision to pull out of the case.
Tang Liang Hong, an unsuccessful candidate for the Worker's Party in Singapore's January 2 general election, fled the city state shortly afterwards saying he feared for his life.
He lost the last of the cases on April 22.

"We feel that Mr Tang needs representation and that's why we are here," Loo Ngan Chor, one of the two lawyers acting for Tang Liang Hong, told reporters on Saturday, outside the chambers of Judge Chao Hick Tin.

Loo and his partner Peter Low on Wednesday asked the High Court to allow them to withdraw from the case after statements Tang made about them in an interview with the Straits Times newspaper on Tuesday.
Tang told the newspaper he was disappointed by his lawyers' failure to file his 60-page affidavit rebutting allegations made against him by PAP leaders.
Loo said that they were going ahead with the case after Tang issued an apology on Friday for the remarks he made to the Straits Times.
In the statement Tang said: "I accept that they used their best professional judgement on the matter. If my remarks are "off-side" in any way, I unreservedly withdraw them completely."
"He (Tang) is under very stressful conditions right now and the comments were made under these conditions," Loo said.
Loo said the affidavit was not filed because he and his partner thought "it does not help advance his case."

The lawyers will be in court on Monday before Choa to determine the costs of damages. More than 30 journalists and all 11 plaintiffs, including prime minister Goh Chok Tong and senior minister Lee Kuan Yew, are expected to testify.
